title: Law Students Found Cheating in Bar Examinations and Steps to Address Public Concerns
what_it_is: Law Students Found Cheating in Bar Examinations and Steps to Address Public Concerns

sections.label: SILE safeguards against Bar exam cheating
sections.summary: SILE added safeguards like remote proctoring, requires cheating trainee lawyers to repeat course or exams, and the Court adjourned their admission hearings after the Attorney-General objected.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: SILE has said that it has put in place additional safeguards to prevent cheating.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It has introduced remote proctoring for examinations that are conducted online and SILE's position is that, apart from the 11 cases which have been uncovered, they have not found any other cases of cheating in the subsequent rounds of the Bar examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As regards these particular trainee lawyers, SILE has required that all of them who cheated are to repeat the preparatory course and/or the Bar examinations in the next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Attorney-General has objected to their applications for admission because of the cheating during the Bar examinations and the Court has adjourned their hearings for admission.

sections.label: Cheating by trainee lawyers serious
sections.summary: The passage states that the offence is cheating, which is serious, and that trainee lawyers make it doubly serious.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The offence here is cheating – which is serious.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Trainee lawyers – that is also serious, doubly serious.

sections.label: Appropriate penalty for trainee lawyers
sections.summary: The passage asks what penalty is appropriate given the offence's seriousness, the trainee lawyers' age, and whether they should be forever prevented from being lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think most people would say that would sound very harsh.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, what is the appropriate penalty, taking into account the seriousness of the offence, but also their age and should they forever be prevented from being lawyers, being called to the Bar?

sections.label: Close supervision and community service
sections.summary: The passage says close supervision is unnecessary at age 23 or 25 to know cheating is wrong, and sees some merit in requiring community service.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As to whether they need close supervision, at the age of 23 or 25, I do not think you need to have close supervision to know that you ought not to be cheating in an examination, because, being Singaporeans, they would have gone through examinations for the most part of their lives and one hopes that this was not earlier practised.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think there are some merits in some of the other points about requiring them to do some service to the community.
